pages.text: 169 In our discussion of the principles of problem solving we considered the problem-solving strategy of introducing something extra (see page 71). In the following example we show how this principle is sometimes useful when we evaluate limits. The idea is to change the variable—to introduce a new variable that is related to the original variable—in such a way as to make the problem simpler. Later, in Section 5.5, we will make more extensive use of this general idea. EXAMPLE 1 Evaluate lim x l 0 s 3 1 1 cx 2 1 x , where c is a constant.
